text: Common injectable vitamin/mineral products: Vitamin ADE, used in cattle and sows (especially after weaning) to stimulate estrus. Vitamin E + Selenium, injected weekly in sows for 3 weeks before farrowing, improves piglet vigor at birth and helps prevent splay-leg. Iron Dextran, injected systematically in piglets 2 days after birth with a booster 10 days later to prevent anemia. Multivitamin products combine B-group, C, A, D, E, and K vitamins, typically injected weekly to help recovery or support thin, multi-deficient animals. Vitamin B12 treats anemia (after bleeding, in stomach ulcers in swine, or with Liver Fluke), often combined with phosphorus (e.g. Carasil) as a stimulant, with iron dextran (e.g. Iron B12) for piglet anemia, or with selenium and magnesium as a muscle tonic for splay-leg piglets (e.g. Biodyl). Calcium can be injected into sows and cows right after delivery when milk production has drawn down calcium reserves, leaving the mother weak, unable to stand, and breathing rapidly.
